standard.title: Specification for Performance of Small Size Spark Ignition Engines for Agricultural Water Pumps, Sprayers, Tillers, Reapers and other Similar Applications
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Automotive Primemovers, Transmission Systems and Internal Combustion Engines

sectional_committee.name: Automotive Primemovers, Transmission Systems and Internal Combustion Engine Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the performance requirements, rating criteria, testing schedules, and wear tolerances for small-size spark-ignition (petrol, kerosene, and gas run) internal combustion engines. It applies to engines of rated output up to and including 5 kW (approx. 6.7 HP) used for driving agricultural water pumps, sprayers, tillers, reapers, and other similar decentralized field applications.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the performance requirements, rating criteria, testing schedules, and wear tolerances for small-size spark-ignition (petrol, kerosene, and gas run) internal combustion engines. version.current_version: First Edition, 1974 (Reaffirmed 2011, Reaffirmed 2016, and Reviewed & Reaffirmed in 2021, incorporating Amendment No. 4, February 2024)

amendments.summary: Minor modifications to fuel testing parameters and scope clarification.
Refines testing fuel grades and carburetor tuning parameters.
Updates engine categorization clauses 1.1 and 10.1 to align with modern commercial agricultural applications.
Substitutes Clause 9.8 'Strip Examination' to mandate a complete post-endurance dimensional and physical teardown of components to assess wear limits against initial pre-testing measurements.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Since IS 7347 is an engine performance standard rather than a safety-critical consumer item, it is certified on a voluntary basis under BIS Scheme I. Successful manufacturers are granted a license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). However, compliance with IS 7347 is universally required by central and state government agricultural subsidy programs, NABARD bank agricultural loans, and mandatory Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institute (FMTTI, Budni) commercial testing guidelines to approve power sprayers, reapers, and tillers.
requirements: Conforming small engines and their packaging must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify baseline quality.

Prior to any run tests, the engine must undergo a thorough initial physical audit (Clause 8.1). Critical component dimensions—including piston clearances, cylinder bore diameters, ring gaps, valve guides, and crankshaft bearing clearances—are recorded to serve as a baseline for wear evaluation.

The engine must be run-in strictly according to the duration and speed profiles recommended by the manufacturer to settle the piston rings and bearings before any power or fuel consumption evaluations begin.

The engine must successfully develop its rated continuous brake power output (kW/HP) at the specified rated speed (RPM) under standard ambient conditions (Roots: BE100K 1.5HP @ 3600 RPM, BE180K 3.1HP @ 3600 RPM; Ralli EL-35: 0.82 kW @ 5600 RPM).

Measures and restricts the mass of fuel consumed per unit of energy produced. For example, the Ralli EL-35 engine is rated for an SFC of 595 g/kWh @ 5600 RPM to verify high thermal and fuel efficiency.

The engine governor must maintain speed stability. When rated load is suddenly thrown off or applied, the governor must react smoothly, restricting transient speed overshoot and settling time to prevent engine runaway or stalling.
Starting tests (using manual recoil or pulley starting rope) must demonstrate that the engine starts easily within a maximum of three consecutive pull attempts under standard ambient conditions.

To prove structural and thermal reliability under harsh farming conditions, the engine is subjected to a continuous or cyclic endurance run (typically 50 to 100 hours of run-time) at rated speed and varying load configurations.

Under Amendment No. 4 (February 2024), at the conclusion of the endurance run, the engine must be fully dismantled. A complete physical and dimensional inspection is conducted on the components checked during initial examination (see 8.1) to calculate physical wear. Component dimensions must not show any undue wear beyond the specified limits.
